name: Familial Platelet Disorder with ANKRD26 Mutation
aliases: Familial thrombocytopenia with predisposition to myeloid malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Platelet Disorder with ANKRD26 Mutation

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with thrombocytopenia in multiple family members
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the ANKRD26 gene by genetic testing
Persistent mild to moderate thrombocytopenia (platelet count typically 50-150 x10^9/L)
Bone marrow examination showing dysmegakaryopoiesis with normal cellularity
Personal or family history of hematologic malignancies such as AML or MDS

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of thrombocytopenia with a pathogenic ANKRD26 mutation and compatible family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; bone marrow biopsy may aid in assessment of dysplasia or malignancy.

laboratory: Persistent thrombocytopenia with platelet counts typically between 50-150 x10^9/L
Normal to mildly decreased hemoglobin and white blood cell counts
Bone marrow showing dysmegakaryopoiesis without overt blasts
imaging: Occasional splenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound in advanced cases
genetic: Heterozygous pathogenic variants in the 5' untranslated region or coding region of ANKRD26 gene
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in RUNX1 gene instead of ANKRD26
Higher risk of progression to leukemia
Skeletal abnormalities absent in ANKRD26 mutation

redFlags: Development of blasts in peripheral blood
references: Noris P, et al. Familial thrombocytopenia with predisposition to myeloid malignancy caused by mutations in ANKRD26. Blood. 2011.
